t: This is the Dutch Church at Austin Friars, a reformed church standing on the site of a thirteenth-century Augustinian friary. The original building was given to Protestant refugees for their services in 1550, and was destroyed in the Blitz of 1940. Several people are buried here. Samuel Hartlib was a polymath of German-Polish origin who wrote on science, medicine, agriculture and education, and who lived near Samuel Pepys. Sir James Tyrrell, a servant of Richard III, is said to have confessed to the murders of the Princes in the Tower. The Dutch surgeon Abraham Cyprianus is also buried here.
